added.title: Full Stack Software Engineer, Travel
added.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s Consumer Verticals team builds experiences that make ChatGPT more useful in the areas that matter to people every day. Within Travel, we’re exploring how AI can help people discover destinations, compare options, and plan trips around their preferences and needs.

Travel planning brings together inspiration, personal preferences, and practical constraints—from budgets and schedules to changing prices and availability. We aim to make that complexity easier to navigate, combining advanced AI capabilities, relevant travel information, and thoughtful product design to help people move from an idea to a trip with greater confidence.

We work closely with product, design, research, safety, privacy, and other ChatGPT teams to turn emerging AI capabilities into useful consumer experiences, with a high bar for quality, reliability, and user trust.

About The Role

We’re looking for a product-minded full stack software engineer to help shape the next generation of travel experiences in ChatGPT.

You will own features end-to-end, from early exploration and prototypes through launch and iteration. Your work will span intuitive interfaces, backend services, and integrations that connect conversational experiences with travel information and services.

This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy shaping new product areas, making complex information intuitive, and moving quickly from idea to production. Prior experience in AI or travel is not required.

In this role you will

Build consumer travel experiences across ChatGPT’s web and mobile surfaces, with ownership spanning frontend interfaces, backend services, and external integrations.
Translate travelers’ preferences and constraints into useful experiences for discovering destinations, comparing stays and transportation, and planning itineraries.
Build integrations with travel data and services
Partner with product, design, and research to turn AI capabilities into intuitive, personalized products and shape what to build next.
Design reliable experiences that handle incomplete information, and service failures while giving users clear choices and control.
Improve quality, performance, and usability through experimentation and user feedback, with privacy, safety, and user trust built into the product.

You might thrive in this role if you

Have 10+ years of software engineering experience, with depth in full-stack development.
Have shipped consumer products at scale and can own features across interfaces, APIs, services, and data flows.
Bring strong product judgment and a high bar for craft, especially when making complex choices easy to understand.
Enjoy shaping product direction and owning ambiguous problems from idea to production.
Move quickly while making thoughtful tradeoffs around quality, reliability, and user trust.
Are excited to apply AI to travel and help people turn their preferences and plans into useful next steps.

Bonus if you have

Experience with AI-powered applications, conversational interfaces, or multimodal products.
Experience building travel, marketplace, commerce including integrations with external providers.
Experience with personalization, search and discovery, or systems that depend on frequently changing data.
Experience with privacy-sensitive products, secure data flows, permissions, or user consent.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

added.description:
What To Expect

Consider before submitting an application:  

This position is expected to start around January 2027 and continue through the entire Spring term (ending approximately May 2027 or later, if available). We ask for a minimum of 12 weeks, Full - Time (40 hours/week) and on-site, for most internships. Our internship program is for students who are actively enrolled in an academic program. Recent graduates seeking employment after graduation and not returning to school should apply for full-time positions, not internships.

International Students: If your work authorization is through CPT, please consult your school on your ability to work 40 hours per week before applying. You must be able to work 40 hours per week on-site. Many students will be limited to part-time during the academic year.

Internship Programs at Tesla

The Internship Recruiting Team is driven by the passion to recognize emerging talent. Our year-round program places the best students in positions that they will grow both technically and personally through their experience working closely with their Manager, Mentor, and team. We are dedicated to providing an experience that allows for the intern to experience life at Tesla by giving them ownership over projects that are critical to their team’s success.

What to Expect

Tesla's Software Platforms team provides the foundation on which the in-vehicle user experience is built. We own the Software Platform (kernel, bootchain, drivers, and lower-level userspace platform services) for the Infotainment systems across our vehicle lineup. This includes high resolution touch displays, high-definition audio, Bluetooth/WiFi/cellular connectivity, USB, cameras - all connected to high performance multi-core processors and GPUs. As a member of the Software Platforms Validation team, you'll be responsible for ensuring that improvements and new features for these systems in our vehicles are thoroughly vetted, building confidence and assessing risks before signing off on each software release.

Join a team of top-notch Software Engineers and Test Engineers committed to continuously improving our vehicles' features and to holding the highest bar for the performance and reliability of our software systems. You will build automation & simulation tools and fleet telemetry pipelines to perform data-based assessments of essential subsystems in our vehicles. You will collaborate across teams, HW and SW as well as Service and Manufacturing, to identify and address critical issues. The ideal candidate is a self-driven and hands-on problem solver, utilizing a range of technologies and strategies to validate and ship our software platforms.

What You'll Do

Work on core subsystems running on the infotainment computer to perform validation reviews and risk assessments before releasing software to the fleet
Write and ship software to the vehicle and build automated systems in the backend to generate and analyze fleet data from the millions of Tesla vehicles worldwide
Define evaluation metrics, create visualizations and dashboards to support the monitoring and refinement of our systems
Build and maintain HIL testers and internal frameworks/tools to accelerate experimentation and debugging of features
Measure and optimize system performance, leveraging off-the-shelf profiling/tracing tools as well as building new custom tools
Work cross-functionally to investigate and fix issues that you identify

What You'll Bring

Currently pursuing a Degree in Computer Science or a related field with a gradation date between 2027 – 2028
Proficiency with one of the following: Python, C/C++, Golang, or Java
Experience with Linux/Unix environments & system administration, CI/CD systems, and large scale data processing & querying
Excellent critical thinking, problem solving, and communication skills
Experience with embedded systems software design concepts and automotive communication standards such as CAN, Ethernet, TCP/IP is a plus
A passion for troubleshooting failures to determine root causes while constantly improving code quality & system efficiency, testability, monitoring, and observability

added.title: Dir/Sr. Dir - Lab Automation Engineer, Discovery Oncology
added.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Dir/Sr. Dir - Lab Automation Engineer, Discovery Oncology

Summary

We're looking for a Director (Principal) Lab Automation Engineer to lead the design, architecture, and software/usability layer of the automated systems that power our NY lab's discovery pipeline. As the senior-most individual contributor on automation, you'll work with the AVP to set technical direction and architecture, partner closely with scientists, software engineers, and platform leaders to translate scientific workflows into reliable, scalable automation — and you'll also get hands-on building the software, tools, and interfaces that make that automation genuinely easy for scientists to use day to day. This is a role for someone who's as comfortable in a scientist's workflow discussion as they are in a systems design review or writing the code themselves — someone who wants to help set the technical direction for automation and build the tools that make it usable.

This position reports to the AVP-Automation, Discovery Oncology and will be onsite in NYC.

Responsibilities

Set technical implementation and architecture for the software/control layer spanning liquid handling protocols and integrated hardware/software systems across the site
Own future workcell design as the platform matures beyond its initial build-out, building on the architecture and standards established during early platform development
Set technical standards and review designs across the automation team, provide hands-on technical mentorship to other engineers without owning their formal management or career development
Partner with the AVP on requirements gathering and vendor evaluation for the most complex automated systems; own installation, validation, and ongoing performance optimization
Lead root-cause investigations for the most complex hardware/software integration failures; drive corrective actions and systemic reliability improvements across the platform
Serve as the primary technical bridge between software engineering, hardware/controls, data teams, and bench scientists to ensure automation and data systems integrate seamlessly
Design and build user-facing tools — UIs, dashboards, CLIs, or AI-assisted interfaces — that let scientists configure, launch, monitor, and troubleshoot automated runs without needing to understand the underlying instrument control code
Build and maintain data capture, upload, and validation pipelines that move experimental data cleanly from automated systems into downstream data processing pipelines and analysis tools
Build monitoring, alerting, and self-diagnostic tooling that surfaces instrument and workflow errors clearly, so scientists and engineers can resolve issues faster and with less escalation
Write and maintain automation scripts, APIs, and configuration templates that standardize how new workflows get deployed onto existing hardware
Advise on vendor relationships and evaluate new instrumentation, technologies, and partnerships to keep the automation platform state-of-the-art

About You

You enjoy working with both scientists and engineers, and can move fluidly between a wet-lab workflow conversation and a systems architecture discussion
You have a solid understanding of data processing pipelines and how automation systems fit into the broader flow of experimental data
You've built tools — using standard programming or AI-assisted harnesses — that make lab automation easier to use, whether that's a UI layer, an instrument control abstraction, or automated data upload/ingestion
You influence through technical credibility and clear communication, not formal authority
You default to designing for the end user (the scientist at the bench) rather than just for the instrument or the codebase; you're a strong software engineer at heart, with enough working knowledge of physical systems to design good interfaces to them

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's or advanced degree in Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Biology, or related field with 10+ years of hands-on experience in laboratory automation, robotics integration, or a closely related engineering discipline, including experience providing technical mentorship to other engineers

Preferred Qualifications

Working familiarity with liquid handling platforms (Tecan, Beckman Coulter/Labcyte, Agilent, Hamilton, etc) and automated imaging/detection systems
Strong programming skills (Python, SQL, and/or C#) with demonstrated ability to build production-quality software, not just scripts; experience with scheduling/control software (e.g. Cellario, Momentum, VWorks, Green Button Go, or custom ACS)
Demonstrated experience designing and qualifying the software/control layer of new automated systems from concept through production
Experience designing user-facing tools (UIs, APIs, CLIs) for non-software-engineer end users
Working knowledge of data processing pipelines and how lab systems integrate with downstream data infrastructure, including experience building or maintaining data pipelines that move data from instruments into analysis/storage infrastructure
Experience building tooling (traditional or AI-assisted) that lowers the barrier for scientists and engineers to use, configure, or troubleshoot automation
Strong cross-functional collaboration skills; able to communicate technical trade-offs to non-technical and senior audiences
Experience partnering on vendor relationships or providing input on project resourcing and trade-offs
Experience applying LLMs/AI agents to instrument control, troubleshooting, or lab software workflows
Experience with Cellario and Cellario integrations
Some background in oncology, mammalian cell biology, or related scientific field
Experience with driver design and implementation
Experience with observability/monitoring tooling (dashboards, alerting, logging pipelines) applied to lab or industrial systems
Understanding of PLCs, safety circuits, and power electronics

Additional Information

This is an onsite position (5 days) in New York, NY
